summary: The Reading School District provides detailed cost-effectiveness data showing how their E-Rate funding has been spent over time, including the impact of special construction and dark fiber support. They argue against sunsetting the program and against limiting eligibility based on geography, competition, or carrier pricing. They support keeping the discount matrix as a graduated instrument and retaining Managed Internal Broadband Services. The district emphasizes the need to control for poverty  The Reading School District opposes sunset provisions for E-Rate funding, citing budget considerations and the need to preserve funding information. The Reading School District opposes the FCC's proposal to condition E-Rate funding on the inclusion of screen-time limits, citing their experience that their current web filtering platforms do not include such features. The Reading School District opposes narrowing the eligibility scope of E-Rate to narrow eligible equipment and services, citing their own cost allocation experience and the impracticality of allocating shared infrastructure by age.
